$comment: Slack's interactivity callback for Block Kit buttons, menus and other actions (type block_actions). Read from docs.slack.dev 'Handling user interaction' and 'Verifying requests from Slack'. Slack posts it as application/x-www-form-urlencoded with ONE field, payload, holding the JSON, and signs the form body as sent. So the delivery is verified over the raw bytes first and decoded second (decode).
title: Slack button click
description: Start when someone clicks a button or picks from a menu in a Slack message the app posted.
summary: a click in a Slack message
setup: In the Slack app's Interactivity & Shortcuts settings, turn interactivity on and set the Request URL to the route your host mounts for this trigger, then put the app's signing secret (Basic Information) on the connection as `signingSecret`. Slack shows the user an error unless the request is answered with a 200 within 3 seconds, so the host must acknowledge FIRST and run the graph after.

verification.$toleranceComment: Slack's guide rejects a request whose timestamp is more than five minutes from now, as a replay. Matched here.
verification.$payloadComment: Slack signs `v0:{X-Slack-Request-Timestamp}:{raw body}`, where the body is the FORM body exactly as received, before any decoding.
